correctness.rationale: The prescribed-center complex harmonic map f has an L∞ circle trace F with |F|≤1, mean c and Fourier coefficients a_n, conjugate b_n. Independent phases turn |a_n|+|b_n| into a real cosine support functional. Adding λc and pairing cos(nt) at opposite signs yields an upper bound I(λ)-cλ via strict square-root concavity; I''(λ)>0 gives the unique λ_c for 0<c<1. The boundary trace (λ_c−2i cos(nt−θ))/sqrt(λ_c²+4cos²(nt−θ)) has mean c and attains both inequalities; strict equality conditions classify all traces, with c=0 sign-cosine and c=1 constants. The standard complete-elliptic K-logarithm and large-λ expansions give B(0)=4/π, B(1)=0, B(c)~2sqrt(1−c) near one, and 4/π−B(c)~πc²/(2log(1/c)) near zero. I checked mean, two Fourier modes and dual optimum independently at 15 center/index pairs. Finite quadrature does not prove all-n/all-c statements.

value.rationale: For the natural Hardy endpoint coefficient problem on the full class of bounded complex harmonic disk maps, prescribing |f(0)| produces a genuinely different exact extremal frontier. The complete function B(c), unique dual optimizer, equality profile at every index, and dissimilar logarithmic/square-root endpoint laws are structural information not supplied by the generic 4/π estimate, and are potentially needed in center-conditioned coefficient or stability questions. This does not conflate one-index sharpness with simultaneous Bohr-majorant control.
